To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
endothelin 1 and endothelin converting enzyme 1 are expressed in lung allograft inflammation and fibrosis.

ET-1 and the ECE-1 are expressed by inflammatory cells, epithelial cells, endothelial cells, and smooth muscle cells of rat lung allographs, and the immunoreaction is stronger than in normal rat lung.
endothelin-1, a potent vasoconstrictor, and endothelin-conveing enzyme-1, which converts big-endothelin-1 to the potent vasoconstriction endothelin-1 are upregulated in rat lung allopgrats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunohistochemical localization and expression of endothelin (ET) and endothelin converting enzyme (ECE- 1) in lung allograft rejection.
the immunohistochemical expression of endothelin (ET-1), and endothelin converting enzyme (ECE- 1) in the lung allograft.
the role of endothelin- 1 and endothelin- converting enzyme-1 in chronic rejection in rat lung al- lografts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ET-1 and the ECE-1 expression in lung allograft are associated with chronic rejection.
ET-1 and/or its precursor big endothelin-1, and/or ECE-1 may be involved in the pathogenesis of obliterative airway disease after lung transplantation.
the expression of ET-1 and the expression of its converting enzyme, ECE-1, is increased early after transplantation and then decreases to control levels as rejection progresses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
endothelin-1 is a potent vasoactive peptide that is expressed in lung tissue.

the immunoreactivity for ET-1 was found in the alveoli and bronchial epithelia, vascular endothelium, and inflammatory cells, whereas ECE-1 immunoreactivity was localized in the vascular endothelum and alveoli.
the immunostaining of both ET-1 and EC-1 in the lung allograft was more intense in the acute and chronic rejection phase compared to the normal lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endothelins may play an important role in chronic rejection of lung allografs.
ET-1 and its processing enzyme, ECE-1, may be important in the pathogenesis of obliterative airways disease after lung transplantation.
ET-1 and ET-1-converting enzymes are expressed in the lung during the early stages of rejection, which is associated with increased expression in the airways and vascular endothelium.
